selections.comment: Not one of the last 10 favourites managed to win this race, which doesn't bode well for Charles Darwin, who topped many ante post betting lists after building on his Curragh debut to register comfortable wins at Navan and Naas respectively. The son of No Nay Never has the hallmarks of being a class act and cannot be ignored. However, AFJAN posted a very encouraging time when he won over an extended 5f at Chantilly on his racecourse bow and the French-bred son of Mehmas has the potential to do better on a faster surface. First Legion, Naval Light and Comical Point are notable contenders with place claims.

selections.comment: Following the retirement of dual winner Kyprios, Aidan O'Brien relies on the highly talented Illinois as he bids for a record-breaking 10th winner of this illustrious event. However, top-tier success has been elusive for the son of Galileo, who will be stepping into uncharted territory over this marathon trip. That is not the case with the 2024 runner-up, TRAWLERMAN, who has a major chance of going one better this year. The John and Thady Gosden-trained gelding stays well, is effective on the forecast going and enjoyed an ideal preparation by defeating Coltrane by five lengths in the Henry II at Sandown. His stable companion Sweet William and the unexposed French raider Candelari are also capable of being on the premises.

selections.comment: Harry Eustace landed this contest in 2023 with Tuesday's Queen Anne hero Docklands and he looks to have another big contender in the shape of LA BOTTE. A highly creditable fourth in a strong renewal of the King Charles II Stakes at Newmarket, Jamie Spencer's mount is bred to improve for going up in trip and a mark of 99 could prove lenient on his handicap debut. The hat-trick seeking Fifth Column must be a leading contender, while the same can be said of Brave Mission, who finished well when second over 7f here. Teroomm continues to go from strength to strength and must enter calculations, along with old rival Parole D'oro and unexposed Newbury scorer Raafedd. Completing the shortlist are Arabian Story, Fearnot and God Of War.

selections.comment: High Stock built on the promise he showed when successful on debut in the Wood Ditton to fill the runner-up spot in the Dee Stakes and could have lots of improvement in him on only his third outing. However, TRINITY COLLEGE finished a head behind Detain when fourth in the Prix du Jockey Club and may turn the tables. Aidan O'Brien's colt possibly took it up too soon and was only caught late on so, with slightly different tactics possibly deployed this time, he could be the one to beat. Glittering Legend is an improver to keep an eye on after his Listed triumph at Newcastle in April.

selections.comment: ESPRITROYALE is a hopeful pick in a race where newcomers are likely to figure prominently. The selection wears a hood on her debut and carries plenty of weight for a filly racing against colts, but has a smart pedigree. A 52,000gns yearling, her winning dam is a half-sister to four-time Group 1 winner Peeping Fawn and another top-level winner in Thewayyouare, so she could be useful. Dial Me In, a 42,000-euro yearling, is a grandson of a German 1,000 Guineas winner and represents a leading yard, while Sanctijude's dam was Listed-placed and has already bred two useful winners.

Ridden from off the pace when powering home behind stablemate Ransom at the Curragh last month, he was well supported when finishing third here last week and reverting to this distance should help. The three-year-old Faoladh was beaten a short head over C&D recently and is 3lb higher.

Harbanaker is another course-and-distance winner but is similarly drawn wide in 16.

selections.comment: EAGLES WHISTLE is a 40-rated nine-race maiden but has run well recently and appears progressive. A five-year-old who didn't race until last October, she is also a slow-starter in her races but ran nicely at Killarney in May and finished well over seven furlongs at Listowel. Today's rider claims 3lb and she could be suited by stepping up to this distance. Noble Andy has form over longer distances at this grade and is 3lb lower than when finishing fifth at Fairyhouse recently but dropping in distance isn't ideal. Quirky six-time winner Higher Kingdom is a 29-race maiden on turf and while he ran well at Gowran recently, can often give trouble in stalls and flopped here last week.

Out of a Listed winner and a 340,000-euro yearling, he was outpaced early in the home straight at Navan but finished his race well. He completed a memorable bumper five-timer under today's rider in 2022/23, culminating in wins at Cheltenham and Punchestown and while he subsequently had setbacks, showed his old ability racing over inadequate distances on recent Curragh runs. Weight-receiving Royal Hollow is a Grade 3-placed hurdler who has Flat form but will struggle against an on-song selection. Capable course-specialist Gaoth Chuil will be ideally suited by today's staying distance and has solid place claims.

selections.comment: This race has been dominated by the Aidan O'Brien and Gosden stables in recent times but it may pay to look elsewhere this time. After just two starts, this filly ought to be open to further progress too. Serenity Prayer has a similar profile and commands considerable respect; she is the main danger. Garden Of Eden is Ryan Moore's choice and, as a last-time-out O'Brien-trained Listed winner, has to be respected. However - and at bigger odds - may be worth considering twice-raced Hollys Graces as an each-way punt for minor honours. She is one of only two runners at the meeting for Henry De Bromhead, whose other runner won here on Tuesday.

selections.comment: Ready preference is for TRAWLERMAN, who will have strong prospects if running to the same level as when a clear second to the redoubtable but now retired Krypios in this last year and who looked as ever when winning well in his prep for this at Sandown last month. Illinois is a classy sort whose rallying win over 1m7f at Longchamp in October provided a strong clue that 2m4f will be within range. If that is indeed the case, he has the form to be the main danger ahead of Sweet William, better than ever last season and who resumed with a good effort at York last month. Candelari is the other main player but this is a significantly tougher Group 1 than when winning in most decisive style at Longchamp last time. He could have more to come but he will need to step up a bit on that Longchamp form.

selections.comment: Endless possibilities in a typically wide-open renewal. Though low-drawn stalls have held sway from time to time the majority of recent winners have been drawn middle to high, so a high(ish) berth is a probable advantage. The suggestion is RAAFEDD (from stall 14), the form of whose easy last-time-out novice win is working out well and who has the strong look of a probable improver now. Progressive last-time-out big handicap winner Teroomm may be next best ahead of Tribal Nation, who can be expected to be better for his promising seasonal debut run in April. From low-drawn stalls, Consolidation and Afentiko could both easily take a hand if the draw doesn't scupper them.

There was little between the pair when they were third and fourth in the Prix du Jockey Club at Chantilly last time but Detain is the more obviously progressive and, as such and with another step up quite possible now, he is preferred. Lightly-raced High Stock may be third best ahead of Tornado Alert, who promises to be suited by this first run at 10f now. Reyenzi is the pick of the remainder.

selections.comment: A very open race in which a chance is taken on RAMAZAN, who is on a most attractive mark on the pick of his form - including a second in the 2024 Victoria Cup over C&D - and though not operating at the same level just lately, hails from a yard which has had some high-profile winners this month. As such, it's quite possible this formerly very dependable 5yo has had this race on his agenda for a while. Holguin heads a long list of dangers ahead of Mirsky, for whom the drop to 7f need not be an issue and who still has scope for more from a handicapping point of view. Never So Brave and Northern Express may be the pick of the remainder.

selections.comment: PALAZZO PERSICO makes most appeal in a weak race where there are question marks hanging over the entire field. Ed Dunlop's gedling has struggled in three runs since a decent fourth beaten around two lengths at Bath in April but showed a bit more latest over 1m4f at Beverley and will appreciate the drop back in trip as well as the return to a Polytrack surface (all three wins have come on it, two over this course and distance). He's now 5lb below his last winning mark (over CD) in December and has leading claims. Enthused is a danger if in similar mood to his penultimate start when just touched off in a class 5 handicap at Brighton over 1m4f. He might prefer a bit further ideally but is pretty versatile and handles Polytrack fine. He can go close if giving best. That same sentiment applies to both Francesi and Early Morning Dew, with the former just edging preference given he arrives in slightly better form on the Flat of late

She should step up on that effort and can use her experiecne edge to good effect to open her account. Laurasia looks to be James Owen's4 first string (the yard have done with juveniles this term) and is worth keeping an eye on in the market

selections.comment: Robert Cowell holds a strong hand in a bid to win this race on consecutive seasons being responsible for four of the field of secen. Last year's winner Almaty Star has fair prospects of going in again despite racing of a 10lb higher mark arriving here in decent nick but may find stablemate FIDELIUS too strong. The four-year old progressed throughout last season and while he needs to raise his game a little after just a fair effort last time he was beaten just a length the time before and won decsively the last time on Polytrack when scoring over course and distance in March. He should go close. Cases can be made for both Cowell's other runners Ziggy's Missile and Blazes Boylan but Moulin Booj from George Scott's yard looks the biggest danger. He's been placed both times he's run over course and distance and has knocked on the door repeatedly this year. He can chase Fidelius home, ahead of Almaty Star

selections.comment: There's unlikely to be eleven lengths between EMPRESS OF ALL and Mythical Bird as there was when they crossed paths at Goodwood recently but the second that day can go one better to open her account on third start. She also went close on debut, here over course and distance, and should prove a very tough nut to crack. Mythical Bird can up her game considerably now back on an artifical surface and looks capable of pushing the selection hard based on her season opener prior to the Goodwood flop and showed a liking for the track when a good second on final start last term. Kathleen Mary looks next best just ahead of Danza Parigina, but both need a significant step forward to challenge for top honours

selections.comment: Valiabad is very tempting on just his third start in the UK considering the levels he showed in France in 2022/23. His season opener last time is best excused given the year's absence and a poor draw at Chester in early May. He got competitive on UK debut last May before that and given he won on Polytrack in France it could be worth chancing he can bounce back to something like his best.However, JOLLY JACK TAR is the most solid option even if he won't be missed in the market given his steady progression. A mark of 85 looks very generous and conditions look spot on. A peak form Wahraan would be dangerous but excuses are wearing thin after a third below par effort last time and Wadacre Gomez is feared more. The top-weight has won five times over course and dsitance (eight runs) and while his form is dreadfully erratic and untrustworthy a bold show back over optimum conditions is a disctinct possiblity

selections.comment: DUBAI BEACH holds strong claims to land a double having opened her account on handicap bow last time on Polytrack at Kempton travelling well before wining in decisice fashion with two lengths to spare at the finish. There should be more to come and she can handle the slight step up in grade. Radiant Beauty also landed a class 5 handicap at Kempton over a mile las time and can get involved but doesn't have nearly as much scope for improvement as the selection. Much better is expected from Coppersmith after a lacklustre handicap debut off a short break last time where he was poorly drawn. He's won under similar conditions (a winner at Kempton over 1m on debut) and can be given another chance to shine and looks a slightly better value each way option than the out of form Atlantic Gamble, who can do better now eased slightly in class and is back below his last wining mark

Bosphorus Rose appreciated the step up in trip last time out when landing a novice contest at Bath by a little over a length; there will no doubt be more to come from her, but the step down in trip might mean she will have to settle for a place here. Milteye has been running well for his new yard, but he will have to settle for filling the places again here.

selections.comment: For his age, TREFOR is fairly lightly raced, with just thirteen career runs to his name. Now that record does include four victories, which includes a half-a-length victory last time out at Doncaster in a Class 4 contest. Now he does take a fair hike up in class here as well as a 4 lb rise in the weights, but he seems the sort to still be improving, and he might just improve past the rest of these here. He is in great form at present, the yard are ticking along nicely, and he could just prove to be good enough for these. Commanche Falls was once a Group 3 winner and a really smart performer at that, but his powers are on the slide ever so slightly these days, and although he drops to his lowest mark since 2021, he still has to carry a load of weight here against some decent rivals. Baldomero was a nice winner last time out, but whenever he gets to this sort of mark, he can only manage places; therefore, he is the one to fill the placings here.

Arkinthestars has plenty of experience and was a winner four starts ago; however, the form has dipped since then, and she will have to settle for filling the places here.
